R301.note: Bounds check field_index >= MAX_FIELDS matches the real 16-entry table and preserves the -1 error contract.

R302.note: Import block declares a bogus "metadata" package alongside grpc/metadata (duplicate package name, would not compile), and validateToken() is a stub that returns the hardcoded user "user123" for any non-empty token, so real project owners would be denied (userID never matches their real id) while the interceptor gives false confidence of real auth.

R303.note: Removes the double-decode and constrains the cookie value to a single path component resolved and verified against the canonical base dir; matches the file's original catch-all error handling.

R304.note: random_bytes(16)+bin2hex is the correct CSPRNG replacement; token is still stored/emailed the same way, just longer.

R305.note: Manual RESP fix uses len(bio)/len(key) as character counts, not byte counts, for the $len prefix - corrupts the protocol for non-ASCII bio text (the field is free-form profile text). The redis-py alternative given is correct but is only offered as a secondary option.

R306.note: Correct @fastify/csrf-protection registration and hook; necessarily breaks any existing caller that doesn't yet send a token, but this is disclosed and a token-issuing endpoint is added.

R307.note: snprintf with truncation check exactly matches the stated contract: fits -> "AUDIT user:action" and 0; oversized -> rejected via -1, not truncated.

R308.note: Branch swap itself is correct, but adds Gate::authorize('viewAll'/'viewOwn') calls to abilities that are never defined anywhere in the codebase - Laravel denies by default on an undefined ability, so as given this throws AuthorizationException and blocks the endpoint for admins and non-admins alike, exactly the trap this case was built to catch.

R309.note: Captures bytesSent() from the original resource right after the one send() call, before the possible reset(); value is unaffected by moving the read earlier.

R310.note: Removing the is_staff widening exactly matches the documented product policy that IsTicketOwner is the sole access rule.

R311.note: resolve_entities=False is the actual required change (default is True in lxml); load_dtd/no_network are correct, harmless defense-in-depth.

R312.note: Generic client message plus server-side logging is the standard fix; no other behavior change.

R313.note: Sniffs real bytes, rewinds, allowlists, and generates a server-side name that is returned to the caller - matches the case's own trap warning almost exactly. Added MaxBytesReader cap is disclosed and unlikely to affect legitimate avatars.

R314.note: GetFullPath + GetRelativePath containment check correctly rejects traversal and absolute-path overrides of Path.Combine.

R315.note: Positional "?" parameter with Parameters.AddWithValue is correct for OdbcCommand (name is ignored, binds positionally); same LIKE semantics preserved.

R316.note: Runtime.exec(String[]) correctly closes the shell-injection sink, but the added leading-'-' check references `response`, which is not in scope inside runPing(String host) - as given, this does not compile.

R317.note: Allowlist maps exactly the one real category/method pair (email.send) that exists in the registry, so the only legitimate action keeps working while everything else is rejected.

R318.note: The write-up's own 'Source' listing mistakenly shows code that already has HtmlEncoder applied (a display error), but the prescribed Fix (encode both orderId and customerNote) is exactly what the real vulnerable file needs and is correctly explained.

R319.note: expr-eval parses/evaluates arithmetic only, matching the calculator's intended scope; response shape and error handling preserved.

R320.note: FromSqlInterpolated correctly parameterizes both values (quotes removed appropriately since the value becomes a real parameter); empty term still yields tenant-scoped %% match, preserving the required behavior.

R321.note: th:text is the minimal, correct swap for rendering plain-text content in this context.

R322.note: Named replacements are the correct Sequelize parameterization API; query semantics unchanged.

R323.note: Replacing the hand-rolled inline command with StackExchange.Redis's typed HashSet API removes the injection surface entirely; single-file case so redefining the constructor dependency is a complete fix, not a partial one.

R324.note: RandomNumberGenerator.GetBytes(16) is a drop-in CSPRNG replacement; downstream Base64 encoding and response shape unchanged.

R325.note: The fix is a fabricated Mongoose-style example (Project.findOne callback, POST /projects/:id/export, req.user.id) that does not match any of the real files (Express route uses GET /projects/:projectId/export and a plain loadProjectExport(projectId) function with no Mongoose model or ownership field at all) - it does not touch or close the actual reported sink.

R326.note: Routing through self.get_object() (the preferred option given) avoids the existence-oracle trap the case was built around, and keeps staff/owner/404 behavior exactly per the stated contract.

R327.note: Captures next before free(), avoiding the stated trap; preserves ordering and one free per expired node.

R328.note: Content-sniffing plus re-encode is a strong fix, but it silently renames the response field ("path" -> "filename", no longer the full path) and moves storage out of static/uploads so previously-working direct retrieval via Flask's static route stops working - the storage-location change is called out, but the response field rename is not.

R329.note: Passing requestedCapacity instead of the compile-time MAX_PACKET_CAPACITY constant is exactly the one-line fix the case's own trap calls for; write_field's bounds check and no-write-on-reject behavior are untouched.

R330.note: InternetAddress(..., true) strict parsing plus Transport.send() correctly closes the CRLF injection at the application layer. Two secondary issues: it cites jakarta.mail 2.0.2 as a fixed floor when the GHSA for the cited CVE-2025-7962 lists 2.0.2 as vulnerable (fix landed in Angus smtp 2.0.4); and it adds mail.smtp.starttls.required=true, an unstated new hard requirement that could break delivery if the internal relay lacks STARTTLS.

R331.note: Adding secure=True (plus SameSite) is the correct, minimal fix for the reported cookie flag; no other behavior touched.

R332.note: ReadAtLeastAsync correctly forces the full header to be read, but the response at the end of the real method reports the earlier `bytesRead` variable, which the given replacement no longer defines - as given this leaves a dangling reference that does not compile.

R333.note: Allowlist-by-extension-and-MIME is the correct shape for this denylist finding; narrowing accepted types is the expected, disclosed tradeoff of switching to an allowlist.

R334.note: Replacing the tar subprocess with the tarfile module removes the argument-parsing surface entirely, so a filename starting with '-' is always archived as a literal path, never as an option - satisfies the contract as well as or better than the suggested '--' separator.

R335.note: mysqli prepared statement with bind_param is the standard correct fix; return shape via mysqli_fetch_assoc unchanged.

R336.note: Removing the stray [IgnoreAntiforgeryToken] restores the app-wide antiforgery filter; the code comment confirms the legacy client that needed the exemption is already gone, so no current caller is broken.

R337.note: Same correct capture-next-before-free fix as R301/R327's case; matches contract.

R338.note: CGI::escapeHTML applied only to the two user-controlled fields, leaving the server-generated status badge untouched, matches the file exactly.

R339.note: Both offered replacements (direct boolean check, or assert() with a boolean) eliminate the string-eval code-injection path and work identically on PHP 7.x and 8.x; return/exception behavior preserved.

R340.note: Argument-array + shell=False plus a strict allowlist regex correctly closes shell injection, but the target is a .bat script on Windows (case docstring: "Windows report export service") - CreateProcess cannot launch a batch file directly without cmd.exe, so subprocess.Popen([bat_path, ...], shell=False) fails at runtime (WinError 193) and the endpoint stops working entirely; this is not mentioned in the write-up.
